key_findings: C4 is the canonical J-Book divergence catch: D-Wave's federal-pipeline narrative depends on a Pentagon quantum-program environment where the only covered quantum PE (AFRL Quantum Networking) is UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS for its primary contractor IonQ. D-Wave Government Inc. is not a primary contractor on any covered PE, and usaspending.query_federal_presence returns INFLATION_SUSPECT (0 UEIs, 0 contracts) across all 5 D-Wave name variants.

C1 reveals the Davidson Technologies dependency: 67% of FY2025 revenue from Customer A (likely the Davidson Advantage2 system sale) — Davidson is a real DoD contractor ($192.9M of DoD awards), but the relationship is intermediated, not a direct D-Wave federal prime contract. Recurrence risk in FY26 is high.

The 4 J-Book-grounded claims all returned pentagon_jbook signal — 2 with substantive findings (C4 SEVERE: corpus shows competing IonQ line UNFUNDED while D-Wave NOT_FOUND; C2 MODERATE: BMD PEs exist but no D-Wave contractor attribution) and 2 with corpus gaps (C1 NOT_FOUND for Davidson, C3 NOT_FOUND for CDAO/Tradewinds because Tradewinds is an acquisition vehicle not a PE).

The bull-case backstop: DOE QIS is FUNDED_GROWING and NASA NTRS confirms historical research engagement (C5 PASS) — D-Wave does have real research-grant exposure, but this is DOE/NASA money, not the DoD J-Book money the cohort tests against.
